recentItems.title: Families cling to hope as 129 remain missing after Indonesia ship capsizes
recentItems.description:
As hundreds of Indonesian rescuers searched the Java Sea on Monday (September 14) for 129 people still missing after a passenger ship capsized, relatives gathered ashore hoping for news of their loved ones.

    "My hope is that my younger brother can be found, whatever condition he's in," said Freddy Manuhua, whose brother was working as a home band entertainer to the passenger vessel. "If he's found in a condition we don't want, I have to accept it because this is the path his life has taken."

    Another relative, still waiting for information on a missing family member, said he had resigned himself to uncertainty. "I've left it all in God's hands. I just hope he is found safe and in good health. Until now, there has been no news," he said.

    Hundreds of rescuers, including coastguard and navy personnel, raced to reach the overturned Virgo Transport 8 on Monday after the vessel carrying 243 people disappeared in bad weather early on Sunday (September 13). Authorities said 108 people had been rescued and six confirmed dead.

    The ship was travelling from Surabaya in East Java province to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan when it capsized. 

    The disaster is the latest in a series of maritime accidents in the Indonesian archipelago. Last month, two ferries carrying hundreds of passengers caught fire in separate incidents, killing six people.

(Camera: Prasto Wardoyo; Editing & Production: Yuddy Cahya Budiman)
